disclaimer: A curated selection reviewed on the date shown, not a complete directory or a guarantee of in-game compatibility. Publisher dates and advertised scope are separate from that review; beta routes and game data can change. Links open the original publisher; no guide packages or addon files are redistributed here.

viewNotes.addons: This is not every addon. Choose the author's Forever file for your actual client and check its dependencies before installing. The combat log is reported closed to addons on Forever, so features built on it, such as Classic-style threat meters, Spy-style enemy detection and cast-bar or aura triggers, behave differently, and Olympus made no install, FPS or memory measurements.
viewNotes.guides: Compare each guide's level range, update date and beta limitations. A published route or build is not a promise that every step has been tested in the current game.

addons.name: Questie
addons.rationale: Quest objectives, map markers and quest tracking.
limitations: The author's Forever work list says quest, NPC and object coverage is still incomplete.
A quest helper, not a complete optimized leveling route.

addons.name: Leatrix Plus
addons.rationale: Optional looting, vendor, quest and interface conveniences.
limitations: Acts for you: only the options you turn on act, and the author says every option starts switched off. They can pick up and hand in quests, accept summons and resurrections, release your spirit in PvP, sell junk and repair at vendors, accept party invites from friends and invite players who whisper you a keyword.
Choose the Forever file; some options differ between game versions.
Enable only the modules you want; features can overlap other addons.

addons.name: Leatrix Maps
addons.rationale: Optional world-map scaling, positioning and map conveniences.
limitations: Select the Forever file and check overlap with other map addons.

addons.name: Auctionator
addons.rationale: Auction-house pricing, buying and posting tools.
limitations: Prices depend on actual scans and your market; not a profit guarantee.
The automatic scan on opening the auction house is Retail-only; on Forever, start a Full Scan yourself.

addons.name: Bagnon
addons.rationale: A combined inventory window and bag searching.
limitations: An alternative to other bag replacements; choose one main bag interface.

addons.name: Baganator
addons.rationale: Categorized or single-view inventory management.
limitations: Requires Syndicator, as the author documents.
An alternative to Bagnon, not a requirement to install both.

addons.name: TomTom
addons.rationale: Coordinate waypoints and navigation assistance.
limitations: Coordinates and supplied routes still need the correct game data.

addons.name: Details! Damage Meter
addons.rationale: Combat analysis for damage, healing and encounters.
limitations: Publisher compatibility is not an independent test of every combat feature.

addons.name: ThreatClassic2
addons.rationale: Threat bars for your group on the current target.
limitations: On Mainline clients, including Forever, the author notes restricted combat data and no healer mode (your target's target).
Forever tank detection uses Defensive Stance, Bear Form and Righteous Fury; Righteous Fury is checked only out of combat.
A mob's threat shows only once you are on its threat table.

addons.name: Decursive
addons.rationale: Spots group members with removable harmful effects and cleanses them from prioritized frames.
limitations: The Forever file is a release candidate (RC4), not a final release.
The author does not say how Forever's restricted (secret) auras affect dispel detection.

addons.name: Grid2
addons.rationale: Party and raid frames built from configurable indicators.
limitations: The developer's claim of lower CPU use than similar addons is not independently measured.
Overlaps other group-frame addons; choose one main raid-frame setup.

addons.name: tullaCTC
addons.rationale: Customizable cooldown text; OmniCC's page points modern clients to it.
limitations: The author says it lacks some OmniCC features, such as Finish Effects and Max Duration.

addons.name: DBM - Deadly Boss Mods (DBM-Core)
addons.rationale: Encounter warnings and boss-mod framework.
limitations: A compatible core does not establish complete new-Forever encounter modules.
For Vanilla and Forever raids, add the separate DBM - Forever and Vanilla pack.
Choose an encounter suite that covers the content you actually play.

addons.name: DBM - Forever and Vanilla
addons.rationale: Vanilla and Season of Discovery raid modules for Deadly Boss Mods; the author says it also covers all Forever raids.
limitations: Requires Deadly Boss Mods Core.
The author says it has boss modules for all Forever raids but does not name them; Olympus has not checked them in game.

addons.name: BigWigs (Boss Timers & Tools)
addons.rationale: An alternative encounter warning and timer suite.
limitations: On Forever its loader uses the BigWigs_Classic pack, whose modules cover only Molten Core, Blackwing Lair and the Ahn'Qiraj raids; no Onyxia or Forever-raid modules were found.
An alternative to DBM; check the author's required modules.

addons.name: RestedXP Guide
addons.rationale: Step-by-step leveling routes and developing dungeon routing.
limitations: Acts for you: the author lists automatic quest accept and turn-in and other automation options; the page does not say which are on by default.
The addon is free; expanded guide packages are paid.
The publisher reported levels 1–35 complete on October 9, before launch. The routes the addon page says come with it are for MoP (1–25), Vanilla (1–20) and Retail (1–10); it names no Forever route.
Check the publisher's current package contents and price; full 1–60 coverage is not assured.

addons.name: Guidelime + TUGs
addons.rationale: Free route-following addon and a separate guide module.
limitations: Also install Guidelime; the addon and guide are separate projects.
TUGs says levels 12–30 were beta-written; 30–60 currently includes a Classic fallback pending Forever updates.

addons.name: Olympus Guild
addons.rationale: A shared in-game view of Olympus guilds, leaders and census reports.
addons.status: Linked to its project page; no file reviewed
addons.sourceKind: Publisher project page; addon API reviewed 2026-10-21
limitations: Optional for website readers; no desktop companion is needed.
Preferred unified guild package; the retired standalone Army ZIP is not offered. Install it from its CurseForge project page. Website snapshot reporting has separate setup and availability.
In-game census coverage depends on reports received by the addon; it is not proof that every guild has a current website report.
addons.integrationNote: The earlier 1.3.2 API review includes permission-gated in-game features and a read-only GetCensusCheckpoint contract; that contract is not this website’s OLCS2 export. The local compatibility patch was prepared against 1.3.2; later releases have separate installed-client and website-export qualification. Publishing the addon does not enable website reporting.

addons.name: Forever Quest Tint
addons.rationale: Highlights quests absent from its original-Classic baseline.
limitations: The author acknowledges possible Classic-baseline omissions; tint is not official confirmation.
Overlaps the quest-highlighting features of ForeverChanges.

addons.name: ForeverChanges
addons.rationale: Highlights new or changed quests, items and spells against Classic.
limitations: Baseline comparisons can be corrected as beta data changes.
Avoid enabling overlapping quest tint effects unintentionally.

addons.name: Forever Goal Tracker
addons.rationale: Long-term goals, step-by-step progress and cross-character tracking.
limitations: Goal inclusion is not proof that every future item or activity is currently obtainable.

addons.name: Forever Quest Pins
addons.rationale: Quest map assistance built for Forever.
limitations: Compare overlap with Questie before choosing your map setup.

addons.name: Forever Statistics
addons.rationale: Character and play statistics for Forever.
limitations: Review the author's local data and export features before enabling them.

addons.name: ForeverForge
addons.rationale: Modular convenience suite with a shared settings interface.
limitations: Acts for you: its Auto Quest accepts and turns in quests at quest givers and can pick a quest reward for you; the author says it is off until you turn it on. Its other automations loot at once, skip gossip, and sell grey items, repair and restock supplies at vendors; the page does not say which of these are on by default. It can also post a chat line when a guild or group member has a newer version, if you choose.
Modules overlap bag, auction, quest and interface addons; select features deliberately.

addons.name: Forever Unit Frames
addons.rationale: Unit and raid-frame interface for Forever.
limitations: Check overlap with your other frame replacements.

addons.name: Lizzarick's Unit Frames
addons.rationale: Luna-style unit frames rebuilt from scratch for Forever and Retail.
addons.status: Author lists Forever and Retail support
limitations: The author says some Luna features are not possible under Forever's secret values and closed combat log.
An early 0.17 release with a small user base; check overlap with other frame replacements.

addons.name: ForeverAuras - A WeakAura Fork
addons.rationale: An unofficial Forever-only fork of WeakAuras.
addons.status: Author says it is still under development
limitations: Still under development; not a guarantee that existing WeakAuras imports work.
Inspect third-party aura code and the author's current limitations.

addons.name: Musca Auras
addons.rationale: An unofficial port of WeakAuras 5.22.0 to the Forever client.
limitations: Acts for you: its optional Announcements pack tells your group about battle resurrections, soulstones and summons by itself; its other packs act only on your click.
Combat-log triggers never fire, and in combat buffs update only through the modern Aura trigger.
In combat, conditions change only appearance; other players' casts and enemy IDs in instances are hidden.
Do not install it alongside another WeakAuras build, as the author warns.

addons.name: ForeverThreat
addons.rationale: A Forever-only threat meter for your current target, with threat sharing between users.
limitations: An early 0.3 release with a small user base; the newer 0.3.7 files are betas.
Keeps no combat history and skips restricted (secret) identity values, as the author notes.

addons.name: TradeSkillMaster
addons.rationale: Gold-making suite for auctioning, crafting queues, mailing, vendoring and bank moves.
limitations: The page does not mention Forever or any limit there; it points to the TSM website for premium features.

addons.name: GatherMate2
addons.rationale: Records where you gathered herbs, ore, fish and treasures and shows the spots on the map and minimap.
limitations: The author notes that original-game node names differ between Retail and Forever.
Pre-filled nodes come from the optional GatherMate2_Data, which the page says now covers Forever.

addons.name: Attune
addons.rationale: Shows attunement and dungeon pre-quest chains and which guild members are on each step.
limitations: Guild progress comes only from members who also run it; it asks their copies only when you press its survey button.
The page does not list which Forever attunements are covered.

addons.name: Spoken
addons.rationale: Plays voiced quest text, NPC gossip, zone stories and books.
limitations: The page calls it AI voiceover with pre-recorded lines and does not say how the voices were made.
Without its voice packs, per module or the English bundle, it is silent; translated quest packs are only on GitHub.
While a line plays it lowers the game music, ambience and NPC voices.

addons.name: What's Training?
addons.rationale: Lists the spells your trainer offers, with their cost, and on Forever the recipes and where they come from.
limitations: The page states no limits; hiding ignored spells at the trainer needs the separate Class Trainer Plus.

addons.name: Pawn
addons.rationale: Scores gear with stat weights and marks upgrades in tooltips.
limitations: Its built-in weights come from Ask Mr. Robot and others; the page does not say they were made for Forever.
It picks the scale for your current spec but equips nothing.

addons.name: Scrap (Junk Seller)
addons.rationale: Sells the items you mark as junk, not only grey ones, and tags junk in your bags.
limitations: Acts for you: when you visit a merchant it sells your junk by itself, and it can also repair your equipment automatically; the page does not say whether repair is on by default.
A community compatibility list notes that Forever merchants already have a button to sell grey items and repair.

addons.name: Prat 3.0
addons.rationale: Chat improvements in 30+ modules: filters, timestamps, history, copying and alerts.
limitations: The author marks settings sync across your account and the spam filter as beta.
The page says nothing specific to Forever.

addons.name: LFG Group Bulletin Board
addons.rationale: Collects dungeon group requests from the chat channels into one sorted, filtered window.
limitations: It recognises English, German, French and Russian requests, and entries drop after 150 seconds.
The maintainer says it updates an abandoned addon and may carry bugs.
Only on your command does it create an LFG chat tab and move the LFG channels there.

addons.name: Layer-Swap
addons.rationale: Shows which layer you are on and lets you ask other users to move you to another layer, or host them.
limitations: Acts for you: hosting is on at every login. It then invites players who ask through the addon, whisper you or ask in your guild, at most six invites in ten minutes, and sets that group's loot to Free for All. A swap request of your own turns hosting on for that request and for four minutes after a successful swap, then restores an earlier off setting. Your request goes out of sight to players on your zone map, and after a swap it leaves the host's group a few seconds later (Auto leave can be turned off), or by itself when the move failed.
It writes nothing in guild chat by itself; Ask your guild sends only on your click.
It reads your layer from nearby creatures, so it must see an NPC first, and a host must be in your zone to move you.

addons.name: Nova Instance Tracker
addons.rationale: Tracks instance lockouts, per-run statistics, gold trades and your alts' rested XP.
limitations: Acts for you: it tells your group when you reset an instance and can post your dungeon statistics to group chat when you leave; the page says that statistics message can be turned on or off, not whether it is on by default.
Its hourly and daily lockout counts and its re-entry detection, which needs mobs nearby, are described without mention of Forever.

addons.name: Altoholic
addons.rationale: Shows your characters' gold, bags, mail, professions and more in one window.
limitations: The author lists one current issue: sharing between accounts does not work.
Its data comes from the author's DataStore modules; the page says nothing specific to Forever.

addons.name: BugSack
addons.rationale: Shows the Lua errors of your session with their stack, ready to copy into a bug report.
limitations: Requires BugGrabber, which captures the errors; BugGrabber's author says it should not be run alone.

addons.name: Simulationcraft
addons.rationale: Exports your character as a text profile for the SimulationCraft simulator.
limitations: The export needs the separate SimulationCraft program outside the game.
The page does not say whether the simulator supports Forever characters.

addons.name: HandyNotes
addons.rationale: A framework for map notes that other authors extend with plugins.
limitations: It does little by itself; the content comes from plugins.

addons.name: RareScanner
addons.rationale: Alerts you to nearby rare NPCs, treasures and events and marks them on the map.
limitations: Forever has no vignettes, so it relies on nameplates, which must be on, and on a scan macro you press yourself.

addons.name: OpenMap
addons.rationale: A seamless, zoomable world map in the original art style.
limitations: The author says to turn off other world-map addons, naming Leatrix Maps, Mapster and Magnify.
Vendors, spirit healers and rares on its map need Questie; the download is 137.9 MB.

addons.name: Atlas
addons.rationale: An in-game browser for dungeon and raid maps.
limitations: The core holds no maps; install a map module such as Atlas Kalimdor & Eastern Kingdoms from the same author.

addons.name: SkillUp Forever
addons.rationale: Shows skill-up chances, recipe costs and colour thresholds in the Professions window, with leveling routes and shopping lists.
limitations: Prices use the cheapest known vendor or Auctionator price, and unknown prices stay unknown.
Some trainer requirements are guessed until a trainer confirms them; the author says it was built with AI assistance.
It keeps an Auctionator shopping list up to date but does not buy for you.

addons.name: Profession Shopping List
addons.rationale: Tracks recipes you want to craft, the materials they need and recipe cooldowns.
limitations: Many described features are Retail systems, such as profession knowledge and crafting orders; the page does not say which work on Forever.

addons.name: Plater Nameplates
addons.rationale: Configurable nameplates with debuff tracking, threat colours and user scripts.
limitations: The page does not say how scripts or threat colours behave on Forever.
Updating scripts and profiles from wago.io uses the optional WeakAuras-Companion desktop app.

addons.name: Threat Plates
addons.rationale: Nameplates that change size and colour with your threat, for tanks and damage dealers.
limitations: The author marks its scripting feature as beta and still restricted.
The page says nothing specific to Forever.

addons.name: GTFO
addons.rationale: Plays a warning sound when you stand in something harmful.
limitations: The author's limits are written for Retail: only spells that apply a trackable debuff are caught.
The page lists Retail and Classic as supported and says nothing about Forever.

addons.name: Skada Damage Meter
addons.rationale: A modular damage meter with several window styles and per-fight segments.
limitations: The page describes the Midnight edition built on Blizzard's session combat data; Forever gets the same file, and the page says nothing specific to Forever.
A community compatibility list notes that Forever has a built-in damage meter.

addons.name: Quartz
addons.rationale: Replaces the cast bars and adds optional latency, global cooldown, swing and buff timers.
limitations: The flight module needs FlightMap or InFlight.
A community list advised against it before this Forever file existed; the page does not describe its behaviour on Forever.

addons.name: Clique
addons.rationale: Click-casting: binds spells and actions to mouse clicks on unit frames.
limitations: Since a 21 June 2026 change you must bind Target and Show unit menu yourself, and bindings cannot be changed in combat.

addons.name: MaxDps Rotation Helper
addons.rationale: Highlights on your action bars the spell its rotation module suggests next; you press the buttons.
limitations: Rotations come from separate per-class modules.
The description dates from Battle for Azeroth and says nothing about Forever.

addons.name: PallyPower
addons.rationale: Lets paladins assign blessings, auras and seals across the group, with buff buttons you click.
limitations: Assignments need the other paladins to run it and leader or assistant rank; its buff buttons do not work in combat.
The newer files v1.6.6 to v1.6.9 are betas.

addons.name: Capping Battleground Timers
addons.rationale: Battleground and arena timers: queue, node and flag timers and final-score estimates.
limitations: Acts for you: it turns in Alterac Valley quests by itself; whether that is on by default was not read.
The page does not say which battlegrounds exist or work on Forever.

addons.name: TellMeWhen
addons.rationale: Shows icons, sounds and text for cooldowns, buffs, debuffs and other combat states you set up.
limitations: The page says nothing specific to Forever; the author takes bug reports on GitHub, not in CurseForge comments.

addons.name: VuhDo
addons.rationale: Raid and party frames with click-healing: spells, items and macros bound to mouse clicks.
limitations: The newer files v3.221-beta-1 and v3.221-beta-2 are betas; the newest full release is v3.220.
Overlaps other group-frame addons; choose one main raid-frame setup.

addons.name: HealBot Continued
addons.rationale: Healing unit frames with click-casting, many skins and action icons.
limitations: The page names Classic and Retail and says nothing specific to Forever; the author advises setting up spells, debuffs and buffs first.
Overlaps other group-frame addons; choose one main raid-frame setup.

addons.name: LittleWigs
addons.rationale: BigWigs boss modules for 5-player dungeons and scenarios.
limitations: Requires BigWigs.
The page does not say which Forever dungeons have modules.

addons.name: Northern Sky Raid Tools
addons.rationale: Raid toolkit: encounter alerts and reminders, aura tracking, ready-check gear and buff checks, and addon version checks.
limitations: Acts for you: it can rearrange the raid group by preset rules and, as an option, share your nickname with your guild automatically; whether these are on by default was not read.
Some features work only if the whole raid runs it; the description is written for Retail and says nothing about Forever.

addons.name: Method Raid Tools
addons.rationale: Raid-leader toolkit: raid cooldown bars, shared notes, reminders, consumable checks, raid inspect, attendance and loot history.
limitations: Acts for you: its invite tool can invite guildmates, accept invites, promote, disband and re-invite; it can place raid marks automatically and turns on combat logging in raid zones; whether these are on by default was not read.
The author marks several modules as only for Classic versions; the page does not say which work on Forever.

addons.name: AtlasLoot Classic Forever
addons.rationale: Browsable raid and dungeon loot tables, best-in-slot lists per class and spec, and a currency tracker.
limitations: The honor rank calculator is marked work in progress for Forever, and the best-in-slot lists give no source.
A fork of AtlasLootClassic; some page captions still name TBC Anniversary.

addons.name: DungeonJournal
addons.rationale: An in-game journal of dungeon bosses, drops, quests and rewards, with an optional no-spoiler mode.
limitations: The author says loot and quest-reward data is still being corrected and asks for error reports; the download is 58.6 MB.

addons.name: Gargul
addons.rationale: A loot-master tool for rolls, soft reserves, wishlists and gold auctions of raid loot.
limitations: Acts for you: with rules you set, it sends looted items to chosen players, rolls need, greed or pass for you, and invites and sorts raid members from a signup; it can also announce trades. The page does not say that any of this is on by default.
The author says that for most features only the loot master needs it.
The author's notes for this Forever release say several fixes are untested because master loot of poor and common items is bugged in Forever.

addons.name: Talents Forever
addons.rationale: The talentsforever.com talent planner inside the game: plan, share and import builds.
limitations: Acts for you: if you choose, it applies a planned build or places your talent points for you as you level; the author says every feature has an off switch.
Popular builds refresh from the author's site every day.
The author says it was built with AI assistance by one person, with talent data from the game files checked in game.
Release 0.38.25 removed a Game talents button that could make action bars vanish in combat; /reload restores a missing bar.

addons.name: Bartender4
addons.rationale: Replaces the action bars with movable, configurable bars.
limitations: Hold-to-cast is not available to addons; the page has no Forever-specific text.

addons.name: Dominos
addons.rationale: Replaces the main action bar with movable, configurable bars.
limitations: The page states no limits and nothing specific to Forever; the author says addons that work on the game's own action buttons should also work with it.
An alternative to Bartender4; choose one action-bar addon.

addons.name: EllesmereUI
addons.rationale: A modular interface suite with a visual layout editor and modules for bars, frames, nameplates, bags, chat and more.
limitations: Several listed modules belong to Retail, such as the Mythic+ timer and Skyriding HUD; the page does not say which modules work on Forever.
It overlaps many listed addons; enable only the modules you want.

addons.name: Titan Panel
addons.rationale: Adds information bars along the screen edges, with built-in and Data Broker plugins.
limitations: The author lists Forever issues with the loot-type plugin and with gamepads.
Since 9.3.0 the author asks you not to drag plugins, as they may disappear on reload.

addons.name: ConsolePort
addons.rationale: Lets you play with a gamepad: bindings, radial menus, an on-screen keyboard and gamepad-friendly menus.
limitations: The page's description is empty apart from picture captions, so it states no limits and nothing specific to Forever.
It needs a gamepad.

addonWatchlist.name: WeakAuras
addonWatchlist.note: No Forever flavor is listed, and Icy Veins reported on 30 Oct 2026 that it does not work on Forever. Alternatives: Blizzard's built-in Cooldown Manager, ForeverAuras or Musca Auras.

addonWatchlist.name: OmniCC
addonWatchlist.note: No Forever flavor is listed; its page says it is supported only on WoW Classic and points modern clients to tullaCTC, which is in the curated list.

addonWatchlist.name: ClassicCastbars
addonWatchlist.note: No Forever flavor is listed; Retail support is paused and the addon is in maintenance mode. A community status table recommends the game's native cast bars.

addonWatchlist.name: Cell
addonWatchlist.note: No Forever flavor is listed and its last release is from January 2026. A community status table suggests Grid2, VuhDo or HealBot Continued; Grid2 is in the curated list.

addonWatchlist.name: Spy
addonWatchlist.note: The original lists Retail only and reads enemy actions from the combat log. The community Spy (Forever) port now has a current Forever release, dated 15 Nov 2026, and detects enemies only through nameplates, target, focus and mouseover. The guild has not decided whether an enemy-detection addon belongs in this list.

addonWatchlist.name: BattlegroundTargets Classic
addonWatchlist.note: Classic only; its last file is dated July 2020, and no Forever build was found.

addonWatchlist.name: Luna Unit Frames
addonWatchlist.note: The official repository supports WoW Classic only and was archived in October 2025. Lizzarick's Unit Frames, in the curated list, is a Luna-style rebuild.

addonWatchlist.name: ForeverAutoQuest
addonWatchlist.note: Its only file is a 2.7 KB release from 18 Sep 2026, before the launch, with no update since. It accepts and turns in quests by itself; ForeverForge, in the curated list, also does this.

guides.name: Wowhead Forever
guides.rationale: Named class writers, talent and gearing reference.
guides.status: Published guides; individual beta scope is dated
guides.scope: Level-30 examples are historical beta references; inspect each current page’s level, build and revision
limitations: Check each guide's date and activity; no final endgame-meta promise.
Some pages need JavaScript to display their full directory.

guides.name: Icy Veins Forever
guides.rationale: Structured explanations for all nine classes and live profession pages.
guides.scope: Page-specific beta builds, levels and changelogs
limitations: Check the date on each guide; the directory's date may differ.
Review and testing vary by article. Do not assume every profession route has been tested through skill 300.

guides.name: WoW-Professions Forever
guides.rationale: Practical leveling routes, material lists, trainers and camping.
guides.status: Published routes with explicit untested sections
guides.scope: Forever professions; later skill ranges may be provisional
limitations: The Alchemy 225–300 route explicitly remains untested under the beta cap.
Material costs depend on your server's actual supply and prices.

guides.name: Method Forever
guides.rationale: Nine class-leveling directories, travel references and available dungeon walkthroughs.
guides.scope: Check the individual route or dungeon page
limitations: Some listed dungeons may not have a complete walkthrough.
Level-60 route outlines may include sections that have not been tested in beta.

guides.name: Mobalytics Forever
guides.rationale: Creator-authored professions, class and patch explanations.
limitations: Distinguish editorial articles from community submissions.
Later profession routes remain subject to beta restrictions.

guides.name: Warcraft Tavern Forever
guides.rationale: Supplemental class and leveling guidance with identifiable authors.
guides.status: Directory listed; article contents not reviewed
guides.scope: Review the article's current date and level range
limitations: The directory listing was found on the review date, but its current articles could not be read. Open the publisher to check their scope and availability.

guides.name: Blizzard Forever Deep Dive
guides.rationale: The announced camping, Legacy, profession and world systems.
guides.scope: Announcements, not an optimized class build
limitations: Later official development notes can supersede announced details.

guides.name: The Forever Era
guides.rationale: Independent data, comparisons and talent/gear tools.
guides.scope: Check build and source labels on each tool
limitations: Its BiS tool discloses indicative weights with no simulations, unscored procs/set bonuses and Classic-derived sources.

guides.name: Classic WoW Forever
guides.rationale: Dated comparisons and system/profession explanations with methodology disclosure.
guides.scope: Page-specific beta build and comparison date
limitations: Discloses AI assistance and a responsible editor.
Recipe counts are dated database findings, not final Blizzard-confirmed totals.

guides.name: Forever Codex
guides.rationale: Additional reference data with source/status disclosures.
guides.status: Accessible fallback is older; live status needs JavaScript
limitations: Do not infer that every page is current with every beta build.

guides.name: RestedXP route progress
guides.rationale: Publisher's dated explanation of the Forever route work.
guides.scope: Publisher reports 1–35 complete; dungeon routing developing
limitations: The playable beta cap limits normal testing above level 30.
Check current package contents and pricing with the publisher before purchasing.

guides.name: Zygor Forever
guides.rationale: Track the publisher's Forever guide coverage.
guides.status: Publisher says Forever guides launched on 3 November 2026
guides.scope: Publisher calls the guides a work in progress, with levels 30–60 still being completed (checked 12 November 2026)
limitations: Check which guides are complete before purchasing; announced features may not yet be available or fully tested.

newsSources.name: Blizzard Forever posts

ownerDirectory.title: The most trusted World of Warcraft: Forever guides and addons
ownerDirectory.scopeNote: The October 18 shortlist records the beta limits and dates known at the time. The October 23 follow-up could not open Warcraft Tavern articles or recover The Forever Era’s BiS method, so those entries retain October 18 evidence. The November 12 follow-up rechecked Zygor and Olympus Guild after launch. Publisher coverage, independent testing and installed-client compatibility each have their own evidence. “Most trusted” describes the shortlist.

sections.title: 1. Where to start
sections.intro: Start with Wowhead and Icy Veins for classes, WoW-Professions for profession routes, and Blizzard for announced rules. Add Method, Mobalytics and Warcraft Tavern for their specific authored coverage.

blocks.heading: Wowhead: named authors and review relationships
text: Wowhead’s Forever team identifies the people behind its class advice. Hunter guides name Docoda and reviewer Neteyes; Rogue names Warstry and reviewer Simonize; Warlock names Zephan, associated with Classic Warlock; Paladin names Surveillant, associated with Light Club. Those are specific relationships, not evidence that every page has independent peer review.

Its level-30 writing-team article and Babyhoof’s Fury overview are dated beta evidence. Match the recommendation to that level, patch and activity; agreement between sites can reflect the same author or model.

blocks.heading: Icy Veins: class explanations and choosing a main
text: The class directory links all nine classes and their specializations. It is useful for learning a playstyle, talent choices and rotations; read the actual author, revision and scope on the selected page. Impakt’s Beast Mastery guide is a named-author example.

The Choosing Your Main guide is an additional starting point. Profession pages are available; the older blanket “coming soon” description is obsolete. A published page still does not prove every later profession step was tested.

blocks.heading: Warcraft Tavern: additional class and system guidance
text: The October 18 review covered named-author class, leveling, class-quest and system articles, along with the publisher’s stated editing standards. Check the evidence and date on each article before using its advice.

links.label: Affliction guide on the October 18 shortlist

blocks.heading: WoW-Professions: practical routes with explicit limits
text: Use its profession hubs for trainer locations, materials, camping and route planning. The Alchemy page still labels its beta-derived plan as work in progress and later materials as estimates. Its Artisan section must not be presented as a fully tested, price-independent route to 300.

blocks.heading: Method: nine classes, travel and available dungeon walkthroughs
text: The leveling directory links all nine classes. The dungeon directory links Hall of Thanes, Ruins of Lordaeron, Excavation Site: Wetlands and City of Dalaran; five additional new dungeons are listed without equivalent linked walkthroughs in the reviewed page.

Its travel article covers boats, zeppelins, trams, portals and Skyborne connections. A route outline or dungeon listing is not proof of completed endgame testing. Assess each guide directly rather than extending the publisher’s general raiding reputation.

blocks.heading: Mobalytics: identifiable creators, separate community contributions
text: Crix’s Alchemy, Engineering and Leatherworking articles provide complementary profession explanations. The October 18 review recorded October 15, 14 and 16 updates respectively; all three pages displayed October 21 revisions when re-read on October 23. Those timestamps describe the articles, not independent testing of every 1–300 step.
Separate editorial articles from user-submitted community builds. Check the particular creator, evidence and later corrections; material requirements and untested later routes remain provisional.

blocks.heading: Blizzard: announced systems and subsequent corrections
text: Use Blizzard’s Deep Dive for its descriptions of camping, Legacy, professions, rulesets and itemization. Later official notes can supersede those announcements. Specialist guides then explain practical choices; neither announcement nor datamining alone proves a tested build or an obtainable item.

sections.title: 2. Class Discords and deeper theorycrafting
sections.intro: Follow identifiable specialists and reproducible work, not a server’s reputation alone. Private Discord content and simulation spreadsheets were not independently audited.

blocks.heading: Use the documented connection, then check the actual advice
text: The October 18 shortlist points to Classic Warlock through Zephan and Light Club through Surveillant’s public writer biographies. These are leads to investigate, not proof that every message, spreadsheet or pinned build targets the current Forever build. No Discord invitation or private-content scrape is embedded here.

blocks.heading: A theorycrafting checklist
text: Confirm an explicit Forever target, game build, level and activity. Identify the maintainer and the evidence: testing, calculations, assumptions or a reproducible example. Look for later corrections.

Check whether apparently agreeing sources share an author, data extraction or model. Repetition does not make them independent confirmations. Unverified claims that all class communities publish reliable simulations earlier than websites are excluded.

sections.title: 3. Independent Forever databases and tools
sections.intro: These are supplementary references with useful source disclosures. An independent database, extracted count or automatic ranking is not a Blizzard certification or a measured final meta.

blocks.heading: The Forever Era
text: The October 18 review describes announcements, beta tables, caches, hotfix information and marked Classic-derived inputs. Use it to compare changes and investigate items or talents.

The October 18 review found indicative weights and Classic-derived acquisition assumptions in the BiS tool. Its method omitted simulations and scoring for procs and set bonuses. Check the current method before using its rankings.

blocks.heading: Classic WoW Forever
text: Its methodology page describes source comparison, corrections and AI-assisted work with editorial responsibility. Use its linked evidence for systems and profession changes rather than assuming extracted recipes establish an optimal leveling route.

The crafting page still displays an October 9 comparison and counts of 860 new recipes and 299 Merchant’s Favor patterns. These are dated database findings, not final availability or a Blizzard-audited launch total. Blizzard’s broader announcement of over 600 recipes has a different scope.

blocks.heading: Forever Codex
text: Its source register distinguishes client records, hotfixes, observations and Classic-derived information, including English and Spanish names. This makes it a useful additional reference when the relevant build is checked.

The accessible status page still exposes build 1.60.1.70245 and an October 8 rebuild while stating that live figures need JavaScript. That fallback does not establish every current dynamic page’s freshness, nor does it prove the whole site is stale.

sections.title: 4. In-game leveling guides and quest helpers
sections.intro: Route planners, quest trackers and paid guide packages are different products. Choose the author’s correct Forever file; the free addon, its guide module and paid coverage can have separate availability.

blocks.heading: RestedXP: evaluate the released package, not its roadmap
text: The addon is free; expanded guides are paid. Its October 9 progress report says the 1–35 routes were finished and dungeon routing was being developed. The author’s release history contains subsequent dungeon updates.

The current product roadmap separately places Forever 35–60 routes after launch, with Era routes available meanwhile; Discovery and Legacy remain planned features. A publisher’s completed-route statement is not independent testing above the old playable beta cap. Check current contents and price with the publisher; no price or exact free Forever 1–20 entitlement is promised here.

blocks.heading: Guidelime plus TUGs: separate addon and guide
text: Guidelime is the route-following addon; TUGs is a separate module. The author lists starting zones, beta-written 12–30 routes and dungeon quest guidance through Dalaran. The page retains a Classic 30–60 fallback while Forever-specific later routes await release. Free availability does not make that fallback Forever-tested.

blocks.heading: Questie: quest assistance, not a complete optimized route
text: Its releases added Forever support and subsequently added and refreshed Forever data, including Zephras Isle fixes. The blanket claim that it has only Classic data is obsolete. It remains a quest/map helper with active corrections, not proof of a finished speed-leveling route or complete coverage of every new quest.

blocks.heading: Zygor: released coverage is still partial
text: Zygor says its Forever guides launched on 3 November 2026 and calls them a work in progress, with levels 30–60 still being completed (checked 12 November 2026). Judge the actual available edition and entitlement before purchase; plans for Skyborne, zones, dungeons, professions and travel do not establish fully tested 1–60 or all-nine-dungeon walkthroughs.

blocks.heading: Install deliberately
text: The preserved addon catalogue below remains a dated selection of general tools and Forever-focused projects. Bag replacements, map helpers and encounter cores can overlap. Check dependencies and client flavor; publisher support is not an in-game compatibility test by Olympus.

Olympus Guild, from its CurseForge project page, includes the optional website aggregate exporter. It is the preferred unified guild package. Website snapshot reporting has separate setup and availability; publication alone does not establish that the installed addon works with this website. The retired standalone Army ZIP is not a replacement recommendation, and publishing the addon does not enable website reporting.

sections.title: 5. How much confidence to place in beta guides
sections.intro: The October 18 review concerned a level-30 beta. Those historical limits explain its examples; they are not a declaration that beta is still playable today.

blocks.heading: Observed gearing advice can be useful
text: Advice based on an obtained beta item can be evidence-based. Complete level-60 loot rankings remain provisional when item discovery, hidden information and tuning are incomplete. Do not turn a useful level-30 example into a final raid-meta promise.

The October 18 review cited a developer interview about undiscovered gear. This directory does not independently certify that interview or any hidden-item model; official announcements and a guide’s actual evidence remain the references.

blocks.heading: Client records need interpretation
text: An extracted record can be real without being intended, obtainable or functioning in the current game. The October 18 review included Blizzard’s October 16 clarification that certain datamined art was not intended for Forever. That dated correction is retained in the accompanying source record; it does not disqualify all datamining.
Similarly, exact-looking recipe counts need their build, comparison method and availability limits. Never replace an unknown measurement with a Classic number or zero.

blocks.heading: Classic routes are labelled fallbacks
text: Classic geography or quest advice may help, but it does not show that new Forever quests, travel, itemization or class changes were incorporated. Keep fallback labels visible rather than presenting an old route as a verified new-game build.

blocks.heading: Seven checks before following a guide
text: Version: does it explicitly target Forever? Scope: which level and activity? Date/build: was the relevant section revised after the change? Evidence: what testing, calculation or assumption is shown? Source labels: are Classic data, estimates and unconfirmed content distinguished? Availability: is the advertised feature actually released? Authorship: who maintains and corrects it?
A narrow class-quest guide need not discuss every new system to be useful. Select for the task, inspect corrections, and keep uncertainty proportional to the evidence.

corrections.claim: Icy Veins professions are all coming soon.
corrections.treatment: Its live profession pages exist; that is separate from full tested 1–300 coverage.

corrections.claim: Method has seven classes and only two new dungeon guides.
corrections.treatment: The reviewed directory links nine classes and four new-dungeon walkthroughs. Listing all nine dungeons does not provide nine walkthroughs.

corrections.claim: RestedXP is a paid addon with every routing mode finished.
corrections.treatment: The addon is free and expanded guides are paid. Published dungeon updates and announced post-launch modes have different availability; the old exact price is not carried forward.

corrections.claim: Zygor already delivers its full announced Forever scope.
corrections.treatment: Zygor says its Forever guides launched on 3 November 2026 but are still a work in progress, with levels 30–60 being completed (checked 12 November 2026). Check actual released contents.
Its author releases include Forever support, base-data additions and later corrections. Individual coverage can still be incomplete.

corrections.claim: An automatic independent BiS score establishes the best gear.
corrections.treatment: The dated October 18 review records missing simulation, proc and set-bonus scoring. Such a score is a candidate-selection aid, not a tuning or final-meta result.

corrections.claim: 860 recipes and 299 patterns are final universally verified totals.
corrections.treatment: Attribute those figures to the dated Classic WoW Forever comparison; Blizzard’s over-600 announcement measures a different stated scope. Neither establishes every recipe’s availability.

corrections.claim: Forever Codex is proven current with every beta build.
corrections.treatment: The fallback identifies build 70245, 8 October, and uses JavaScript to load live figures. Check the date and build on the page you plan to use.

corrections.claim: All prelaunch gearing advice is only guessing.
corrections.treatment: Observed items can support useful advice. Unknown gear and future tuning limit complete endgame rankings; retain each recommendation’s evidence and scope.

corrections.claim: Every named source is peer-reviewed, most complete, or independently simulated.
corrections.treatment: Those blanket endorsements were not established. Follow identified authors, explicit reviewer relationships, changelogs and disclosed methods. The October 18 review also noted a sponsorship/affiliate disclosure in an older comparison; its dated judgments are not imported as independent confirmation.
